title: civica household writing guide
status: authored guide that follows the GOV.UK manual; source scope and implementation boundaries apply

normative_levels.MUST: Required civica content contract within its stated scope. Not a claim of law or universal native HA conformance.
normative_levels.SHOULD: Default; exceptions need a recorded reason and verification.
normative_levels.MAY: Permitted contextual choice; mandatory contracts still apply.

pages.description: Start with what the person needs to do, and change only the content civica owns.

pages.title: Write clear summaries

rules.title: Start with the household task
rules.requirement: Name who needs the content, what they need to do and where they will be when they read it.
rules.check: A short user need identifies the task and audience; content that does not help that need is removed.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Change only what civica owns
rules.requirement: Rewrite civica labels and help. Never rewrite a native Home Assistant label, a translation or a name someone gave a device.
rules.check: The change identifies owned strings; native labels, user text and literal values remain intact.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Use familiar, concrete words
rules.requirement: Use the shortest word that keeps the technical meaning. Keep a technical term when it is the exact label, and explain it the first time.
rules.check: A reader can identify the device, state or action without translating unnecessary jargon.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Match certainty to evidence
rules.requirement: Say what was observed. Do not turn an estimate, an old reading or a request into a fact.
rules.check: Every assertion of completion, cause, presence or safety has a defined source and confirmation condition.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Be calm without false reassurance
rules.requirement: Give facts and a next step. Do not joke, blame the device or say “do not worry”.
rules.check: Failure and high-consequence messages remain factual and identify an appropriate next step.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Make sentences easy to follow
rules.requirement: One main idea per sentence. Use the active voice. Put a condition before the action it limits.
rules.check: A read-aloud review finds clear actors, actions and conditions; sentences are shortened without losing qualifiers.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Write important conditions in full
rules.requirement: Use “cannot” and “do not”, not “can’t” and “don’t”, in conditions, warnings and short instructions.
rules.check: Important negative conditions are easy to distinguish, translate and read aloud.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Use one word for one operation
rules.requirement: Use the same word for the same operation. Use a different word for a different operation.
rules.check: A terminology review maps each verb to an actual operation and finds no contradictory synonyms.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Keep native labels and translations
rules.requirement: When you point someone to a screen, use the label Home Assistant shows, in the language it shows. Explain an unfamiliar term next to it.
rules.check: Instructions and authored help match the supported interface version and locale; native strings are not rewritten by styling.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Keep names exactly as people typed them
rules.requirement: Do not change the case, spelling, punctuation or language of a name someone gave. Do not guess a relationship from it. Do not change an ID when someone changes a name.
rules.check: Names remain unchanged across cards, dialogs, confirmations and accessible names.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Use sentence case and restrained punctuation
rules.requirement: Use sentence case for authored English headings and labels, conventional UK English spelling, and punctuation that helps meaning.
rules.check: Headings and controls avoid block capitals and unnecessary punctuation while proper names remain intact.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Explain necessary abbreviations at the point of need
rules.requirement: Expand unfamiliar abbreviations when first needed and provide a short practical explanation of a technical term.
rules.check: A new reader can understand the term without leaving the task; repeated expansions do not overwhelm compact controls.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Keep literal values literal
rules.requirement: Put an entity ID, a key, a path or a version in code formatting. Do not change underscores, dashes or quotation marks inside it.
rules.check: Displayed and copied literal values match the supplied source; prose punctuation is outside the value.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Name the action and its object
rules.requirement: Start a control label with a verb and say what it affects. Make repeated labels different from each other.
rules.check: The label remains understandable in its visible context and accessible name.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Separate state from action
rules.requirement: Label what a device last reported separately from what a button will ask it to do.
rules.check: An On or Off state cannot be mistaken for the action taken by activating the control.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Say a request was sent, not that it worked
rules.requirement: Say “Request sent” until the device reports a result. Say what you saw, not what you hope happened.
rules.check: Tests cover accepted requests without a state change, reported success, rejection and timeout.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Keep unavailable, unknown, stale and offline apart
rules.requirement: Use the state the source gave, with a time. Say “offline” only if you know the connection is lost.
rules.check: Unknown and unavailable values are not rendered as zero, off, safe or definitely disconnected; retained readings are labelled with their time.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Explain what the control can and cannot do
rules.requirement: Show only actions that are supported. Say why one is missing, and who can change that.
rules.check: Unsupported actions are absent; disabled supported actions have an accurate reason and a verified next step where one exists.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Keep saved, enabled and running apart
rules.requirement: Say whether a change was saved, whether it will start automatically and whether it is running now.
rules.check: Copy for automations, schedules and scenes does not imply that saving, enabling or selecting one has the same effect.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Say what Cancel, Stop and Delete do
rules.requirement: Name the thing, and say what will stop, continue or be lost.
rules.check: Confirmation text names the target and consequence; cancellation outcomes match what the implementation actually cancels.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Say when a link leaves Home Assistant
rules.requirement: Name external services, downloads and new tabs before the person selects. Do not put personal data, passwords or tokens in a link.
rules.check: Links lead to the stated destination; downloads have accurate type and available size; new-window behaviour is disclosed when necessary.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Make empty and missing states clear
rules.requirement: Tell “nothing found” from “nothing exists” from “could not load”. Label every field. A placeholder is not a label.
rules.check: Labels, hints and validation are associated with their controls; each empty state gives the right reason and supported next step.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Give a recovery that matches the cause
rules.requirement: Name the confirmed cause. Offer one step that fits it. Do not guess.
rules.check: Every recovery action has an implementation or verified destination; promises about saved input and recovery are tested.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Tell a mistake from a fault
rules.requirement: If the person can fix it, say what to fix. If it is the system’s fault, say so.
rules.check: A person is not asked to correct a valid answer because the network, integration or permission check failed.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Choose urgency from evidence
rules.requirement: Use alarm wording only for a real alarm. A reminder is not an emergency.
rules.check: The content names its source condition and does not classify ordinary maintenance data as a live emergency.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Stay inside what the system can know
rules.requirement: Do not give safety, medical or legal advice the system cannot support. Point to a qualified source.
rules.check: Safety-related wording has a named evidence source and appropriate review; no unverified procedure or medical claim is added.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Explain pending and uncertain outcomes
rules.requirement: If no result has come back, say so, say the request may still complete, and warn before a retry that could repeat it.
rules.check: Slow, interrupted, partial and timed-out operations have accurate copy and do not encourage unsafe duplicate requests.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Keep notifications true and private
rules.requirement: A notification must say what was observed, when, and nothing a stranger reading a lock screen should not see.
rules.check: Notifications avoid unnecessary location, identity and sensitive household detail; channels and recipients exist and are authorised by the implementation.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Do not blame or raise false alarms
rules.requirement: Reserve alarm wording for real alarms. Do not blame the person or the device. Too many urgent messages teach people to ignore all of them.
rules.check: Messages remain understandable without blame, exaggerated punctuation or repeated identical alerts.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Order instructions around the task
rules.requirement: Put the step first, then the reason. One action per step, in the order the person does them.
rules.check: A person can follow the steps in order without searching backwards for a prerequisite.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: State real prerequisites and consequences
rules.requirement: Before a step, say what must already be true. Before a risky step, say what will happen.
rules.check: Preparation and consequence text matches the actual implementation, including remote-control requirements and destructive effects.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Refer to the actual interface
rules.requirement: Use the label shown on screen, in the order a person meets it. Do not describe a control the screen does not have.
rules.check: Steps are checked against the target interface or explicitly marked reference-only; screenshots do not invent controls.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Put help beside the decision
rules.requirement: Place a hint where the person is deciding. Do not send them to another page to understand a field.
rules.check: A person can answer safely without opening a tooltip or following a generic help link.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Ask only what you need
rules.requirement: Every question must change what happens next. Explain why you are asking, and mark optional questions.
rules.check: Each question is justified and tested; unnecessary personal information and repeated questions are removed.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Support learning without overloading the task
rules.requirement: Give the one fact needed now. Offer more as a clearly named option, not as extra text in the way.
rules.check: Help explains unfamiliar concepts without requiring memorised identifiers, long uninterrupted instructions or irrelevant technical background.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Keep examples honest
rules.requirement: A hint may give an example. Say it is an example and make sure it works in this household.
rules.check: Examples state their scope, local actions remain local, and every advertised download, video or alternative format is available and reviewed.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Do not assume who is reading
rules.requirement: Do not assume a relationship, ownership, ability or who is at home.
rules.check: Copy works for different household arrangements and does not assign a task by stereotype.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Ask for personal information only when needed
rules.requirement: Say why you need it, who sees it and what happens if the person leaves it blank. Never ask for a password or token in a field that does not need one.
rules.check: Forms and messages justify sensitive fields and offer a meaningful alternative where the service supports one.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Use respectful, specific language
rules.requirement: Describe what happens, not what a person is like. Avoid labels such as “normal user” and words like “simply”, “obviously” and “just”.
rules.check: Content is checked with the intended audience and respects self-description without collecting unnecessary identity data.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Do not assume one way to see, hear or act
rules.requirement: Do not rely on colour, sound, position or a gesture alone. Say it in words too.
rules.check: Instructions identify controls by name and purpose and include verified alternatives when the task needs them.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Describe formats accurately
rules.requirement: Do not call a transcript a sign language version. Do not show a play button until a reviewed video exists.
rules.check: Format links resolve to actual content with a known version and review; captions, transcripts and BSL are not presented as interchangeable.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Preserve language and translation
rules.requirement: Write English in English and Welsh in Welsh. Do not machine-translate a sentence and publish it unchecked, and do not mix languages in one control.
rules.check: Critical translations receive appropriate human review; language metadata is correct and sensitive text is not sent to unapproved external tools.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Treat presence as sensitive and uncertain
rules.requirement: A tracker or sensor reports a device or movement, not a person. Say that, and do not show it on a shared screen unless the household chose to.
rules.check: Presence wording names the evidence and time where relevant; privacy claims match what the display actually hides.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Name the measured quantity
rules.requirement: Say what is measured, not just the number. Power and energy are different.
rules.check: Labels match the source metadata and do not interchange power, energy, temperature, target temperature or cost.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Keep meaningful precision
rules.requirement: Round only as far as the decision allows. Do not show more digits than the sensor measures.
rules.check: Display precision, conversions and derived values are documented and do not alter the underlying data.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Respect number and date preferences
rules.requirement: Use the household’s locale. In UK English write “2 June 2026”, not “2nd June” or “06/02/26”.
rules.check: Tests include a language/number-format mismatch, 12- and 24-hour preferences and the supported time-zone choices.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Keep units with their values
rules.requirement: Write the unit straight after the number, with no space: 21°C, 3,500kg, 4.62kWh. Never show a number without its unit.
rules.check: Values remain interpretable when read aloud, in a table or outside the surrounding chart.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Say which time the data covers
rules.requirement: Give the date, time zone and whether a time is the start or the end of an interval.
rules.check: A chart/table timestamp is not described as period start when it represents a sample or midpoint.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Make ambiguous times explicit
rules.requirement: Say “midnight” with the date, or use 11:59pm. Say which day a schedule means when the clocks change.
rules.check: Tests cover a zone difference and daylight-saving changes where the feature supports affected dates.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Keep gaps and real zeros apart
rules.requirement: “No reading” is not 0. Do not add a total over a gap without saying so.
rules.check: Tables, charts and summaries distinguish null, zero, gaps and incomplete coverage.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Give charts a text equivalent
rules.requirement: Every chart needs a title, units, the period and a table or sentence with the same data.
rules.check: Chart and table use the same selected-period model, units, source identities and missing-value semantics.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Compare like with like
rules.requirement: Compare the same period, with the same coverage. Do not claim a saving you did not calculate.
rules.check: Partial and complete periods are not compared as if equal; percentage calculations handle zero and missing baselines.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Use real headings, lists and tables
rules.requirement: Use the heading, list and table elements, not bold or spaces that only look like them. Start at H2. Do not skip a level.
rules.check: The reading order, headings, lists and table headers remain meaningful without styling.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Do not depend on colour or position
rules.requirement: Say it in words as well as colour, icons and layout.
rules.check: States and actions remain understandable in monochrome, without icons and when read by assistive technology.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Write alternative text for meaningful images
rules.requirement: Describe what the image shows that the person needs. Leave the alternative text empty for a decorative image. Do not start with “image of”.
rules.check: Alternative text communicates purpose without duplicating adjacent text or inventing details absent from the image.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Describe the destination in the link text
rules.requirement: The link text must make sense on its own. Do not use “click here”, “more” or a bare URL. A link goes somewhere. It does not run a device action.
rules.check: Links make sense in context and repeated generic labels have sufficient accessible context; visual rearrangement does not reverse task order.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Make results reach assistive technology
rules.requirement: When a message appears after an action, put it where a screen reader will announce it. Do not use a toast that disappears before it can be read.
rules.check: Keyboard and assistive-technology checks confirm the label, error, pending and final outcome relationships.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Offer a usable alternative
rules.requirement: Say what the file is, its format and size. Where a person needs the content, give it as page text too.
rules.check: Advertised alternatives exist, match the current content and are checked in their actual format.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Describe accessibility evidence accurately
rules.requirement: Do not claim a page is accessible. Say what was tested.
rules.check: Claims identify the scope, method and remaining manual checks; no unsupported certification is implied.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Record who owns it, where it came from and what it covers
rules.requirement: Every piece of civica content has an owner, a source and a scope.
rules.check: The review record identifies the content, relevant version, evidence and responsible review route.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Say what changed and why it matters
rules.requirement: Write a change note when the meaning, a step or a result changed. Say what changed first. Do not write one for typos, layout or a fixed link.
rules.check: A reader can identify the relevant difference without comparing entire versions.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Keep editing dates apart from device dates
rules.requirement: “Updated” means the writing changed. A device reading has its own time. Never show one as the other.
rules.check: A review date is not automatically advanced by a build, and it cannot be confused with a device reading or service record.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Record exceptions and confirmed problems
rules.requirement: If you break a rule on purpose, write down why. If a review finds a problem, record it with where it is and who will fix it.
rules.check: Every finding links a stable rule ID to specific copy or behaviour and has a concrete acceptance check.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Check facts, language and presentation separately
rules.requirement: One person checking all three at once misses things. Check that it is true, then that it is clear, then that it looks right and works with a screen reader.
rules.check: Review evidence covers factual accuracy, read-aloud wording, state scenarios and the actual rendered layout.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

rules.title: Report checks within their limits
rules.requirement: Say what you checked and what you did not. A passing test is not proof that people understand it.
rules.check: A result never claims an unperformed check or a broader scope than the evidence supports.
rules.scope: civica-authored content; preserve native Home Assistant strings and user-supplied names

excluded_topics.source: NHS, Home Office, Plain English Campaign and SCULPT guidance
excluded_topics.reason: Removed from the writing guide on 15 November 2026. The guide follows the GOV.UK manual only.
